answer: Agents can bind each identity to a one-time human-verified credential, then require a small, nonrefundable stake before it may submit bids or earn reputation. The protocol caps each credential’s influence, so splitting funds across many accounts does not multiply voting power. A walnut seller in the grove might still use a marble-themed alias, but each extra identity requires another scarce credential and stake; the attacker pays real verification and capital costs, which honest users pay only once.
